content: How do I implement secure JWT authentication with refresh token rotation in a Python FastAPI application?

To implement secure JWT authentication with refresh token rotation in FastAPI, you will need two tokens: a short-lived access token (e.g., 15 minutes) and a longer-lived refresh token (e.g., 7 days) stored securely in an HttpOnly cookie or database.
What cryptographic algorithm should I use for signing the tokens? Is RS256 preferred over HS256?

RS256 (asymmetric RSA) is preferred in microservices where multiple downstream services verify tokens using a public key without needing the private signing key. HS256 (symmetric HMAC) is simpler if only a single authentication server verifies tokens.
Can you provide code for the password hashing helper using bcrypt or argon2?
Here is how you can use passlib with argon2 or bcrypt for FastAPI password hashing with CryptContext.
How should I structure the token payload? What standard claims should I include?
Standard claims to include in the JWT payload: sub (user ID), exp (expiration timestamp), iat (issued at), nbf (not before), iss (issuer URL), and jti (unique token identifier for revocation).
